title: Follow one source
text:
Change **SOURCE** at DRESS THE ARCHITECTURE. Look for a recognisable part of the selected machine's output on both floor and wall.

This controller passes an image to the architectural surfaces. It changes their appearance; their physical support stays in place. The small tile stations have separate previews.
source: technical.md / Whole-hall print and the local floor

title: One address, many appearances
text:
Place two differently coloured marks beside one another, away from the centre of the small tile. Find the pair in several repeats. Then change just one of those two source cells.

The source is a finite array. Each preview position is mapped back to a source address. One edited address can therefore alter many visible places.

title: Give the rule something to reveal
text:
Keep the pair asymmetric. Compare its direction under simple repetition and reflection. A centred dot can conceal a reversal.

Keep the distinction in view: **the motif** is the arrangement you authored; **the repetition rule** decides how its copies appear. Changing either can change the field.

title: The same address on a bent sheet
text:
The two samples share the same colour image and texture addresses. Each sheet measures 1.2 metres across its surface. On the curved sample, measure along the arc.

Walk sideways before deciding that the mark itself has narrowed. Its projection into your view has changed.
source: technical.md / Live comparison; tutorial.md / second paragraph

title: Keep a surface at an earlier moment
text:
With **CURVE** selected, press **LINK / HOLD**, then **MARK**. Compare the samples.

The held curve declines the next image. Its whole image stays; this does not give one repeated mark an independent source. Link it again to receive the current image.

title: Try the same separation around your body
text:
Inside the curved room, paint a cell at the studio. Its wall and floor start linked to that source.

Select **ROOM FLOOR**, press **HOLD**, then edit the source again. The wall should follow; the floor should keep its earlier print. **APPLY LIVE** reconnects it.

This room and the larger hall have separate source connections.
